events.title: COBOL language finalized
events.summary: In December 1959, a committee of government and industry experts finalized COBOL — a business programming language meant to work on any mainframe.
events.about: COBOL was for business records on mainframes — readable English-like syntax for payroll, banking, insurance, and government systems. Example jobs: processing millions of transactions, printing statements, and batch reporting. A large share of global financial back-office code still runs on COBOL.

narrative.whyChosen: COBOL gave banks, insurers, and government agencies one readable language for payroll, billing, and record-keeping — instead of a different dialect on every computer.
narrative.whyImportant: U.S. defense procurement pushed vendors to support it, proving a shared business language could run across competing hardware.
narrative.problemSolved: Every computer maker had its own data-processing language; businesses couldn't move software between machines.

sources.title: CODASYL — COBOL Report (April 1960, specs dated Dec 1959)
